sections.h2: What is Hart County, Georgia, and who handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Hart County is lake country in the northeast corner of Georgia, right beside I-85. Hartwell is the county seat, Lake Hartwell supplies 222 miles of shoreline, and Exit 177 on I-85 is about an hour and a half from Atlanta. Federal figures list 232 square miles of land and 28,639 residents as of 2025.

Hart County was formed in 1853 from parts of Elbert and Franklin counties and is the only Georgia county named for a woman, the Revolutionary War figure Nancy Hart. Gateway Industrial Park sits at the I-85 exit, and the county shares an airport and an animal shelter with Franklin County. The county's own profile cites about 49 inches of rain a year, with summer averages near 89 degrees and winter averages near 57, which is the climate any buyer's inspector will be reading a house against.

  • Board of Tax Assessors: P.O. Box 810, Hartwell, GA 30643, 706-376-3997. Values property, takes homestead applications and handles appeals.
  • Tax Commissioner: in the courthouse in Hartwell. Collects property tax, auto tags, timber payments, mobile home tax and the intangible recording tax.
  • Records: the county website links to a property tax record search and to an online payment site.

sections.h2: When are Hart County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Hart's assessment page describes a December 20 deadline in a normal year, with state law holding off interest for 60 days after mailing. Whatever your bill prints is the date that counts.

Georgia's revenue department puts it the same way: December 20 is the official statewide due date, a county can move it to December 1 or November 15, and a bill carries a 60 day grace from the postmark. Penalties can attach to delinquent taxes on top of interest. Hart County's tax commissioner has added a drop box outside the courthouse for property and auto payments, and an online payment option is linked from the county website.

Mobile homes follow a separate schedule. A mobile home standing in Hart on January 1 must be returned to the Tax Commissioner by May 1, and the yearly location permit window is January 1 to May 1 as well. A newly placed home needs a permit within 30 days. Ask the Tax Commissioner when the tax on a mobile home account falls due.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Hart County assessment?
sections.html:
Hart wants the appeal postmarked inside 45 days of the date on the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. That notice goes out when they disagree with the value you returned.

Hart County states that every parcel is reevaluated each year, and a tax notice is sent out each year by April 15. Owners in Hartwell and on the lake shore should read that notice as soon as it arrives, because the 45 day appeal clock starts from the notice date. The assessors' office will explain the filing procedure by phone.

Another route runs through the return. A return can be filed with the assessors from January 1 through April 1. The tax commissioner's page tells owners who think their value is too high to file a return reducing it by April 1 in order to have a chance at a lower value for the next year's taxes. The state revenue fact sheet gives three years from payment to claim back tax that was wrongly or illegally collected, with a written claim to the county governing authority.

sections.h2: What homestead and exemption rules apply in Hart County?
sections.html:
Hart expects the homestead filer to live in the house as a legal residence, and the paperwork goes to the assessors' office. A person away for health reasons will not be denied, and a family member or friend can notify the office on their behalf.

  • Owning the property on January 1 and filing by the April 1 return date secures the exemption for that tax year.
  • Certain elderly owners qualify for additional exemptions beyond the regular homestead. The Tax Commissioner's page urges eligible owners to apply by April 1 so the benefit carries into later years.
  • Call the assessors at 706-376-3997 to ask whether a local homestead exemption sits on top of the state ones for your parcel.

Timing matters in the sale year. A buyer who moves in after New Year's files for a personal exemption later, and the seller's old filing does not follow the seller to a new address. The state revenue sheet treats skipping the application as a waiver.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers show for Hart County housing?
sections.html:
Hart County is affordable by Georgia standards. Survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a middle owned home of $215,100, a middle rent of $844 and 77.8% of homes occupied by owners.

Population rose 10.9% from the April 2020 base to the 2025 estimate, and about one resident in four is a senior. With 13,800 housing units against 11,034 households, the county has more homes than households. Owners of a house that sits empty part of the year should ask both offices whether an exemption they hold still applies.

sections.h2: What local features shape a Hart County sale?
sections.html:
Lake Hartwell drives much of the local market. The county profile highlights its parks, camp sites, marinas and boat ramps, and annual events such as the Antique Boat Festival and a dam run. Hartwell itself has historic homes near a downtown shopping district, and the county reports a 74 bed hospital with a 24 hour emergency room, which matters to the many retirees in the Census figures.

Daily travel runs on the roads and I-85. Hart Transit offers local rides on weekdays at 706-376-3975, and Clemson, Athens and Anderson are all within commuting range according to the county profile. A shoreline lot, a farmhouse and a Hartwell bungalow can each raise different tax questions, from acreage covenants to homestead, so gather the parcel number before calling either office.

sections.h2: What should a Hart County seller know about recording and closing costs?
sections.html:
Hart County's Tax Commissioner collects the intangible recording tax. A lender holding a long-term note on real estate has 90 days to record the security instrument locally. The charge is $1.50 per $500 of the note, rounded up for any fraction.

A seller mostly needs the property tax payoff and a clean title. The county homepage lists 185 West Franklin Street in Hartwell as the overnight and physical address for the Clerk of Superior Court, who handles recording, and it notes that mail to the office had been coming back from the post office.

Before listing a Hart County house, gather your latest assessment notice, the most recent tax bill, any mobile home permit records and any covenant paperwork. Get the unpaid balance from the Tax Commissioner, then settle with the closing attorney who carries this year's bill.

faqs.q: When are Hart County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Hart describes December 20 as the normal deadline, and state law holds off interest for 60 days after mailing. Go by the date on your bill.

faqs.q: How soon must a Hart County appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Postmark it within 45 days of the change-of-assessment notice, addressed to the assessors. Phone 706-376-3997 for the steps.

faqs.q: When is the Hart County homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. You need to have owned and lived in the house on January 1, with the form at the assessors' office by the return deadline.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Hart County mobile home tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Tax Commissioner. The return and the yearly location permit both fall between January 1 and May 1, and whoever owned the home there on January 1 files.

faqs.q: Does Hart County reassess every year?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says it reevaluates every parcel each year and sends notices by April 15, with 45 days to appeal a value you dispute.
